negative_findings.description: No Hungarian-language or English evidence surfaced of a Temenos, Backbase or Finastra implementation at OTP, Erste or MBH, despite these being the cell's named seed vendors.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned only vendor-vs-vendor comparison marketing. The HU core/digital stack that did surface is different: Oracle Flexcube (MKB/MBH), Intellect iGCB (OTP core revamp), Tietoevry (OTP card acquiring), valantic (Erste instant payments), Finshape/BSC-W.UP (digital channels).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's seed vendor list is partly wrong for Hungary. Monitoring effort should be reallocated to the vendors actually present, or the pointer value of Temenos/Backbase/Finastra pages will be near zero.

negative_findings.description: No Hungary country-manager or country-lead appointment announcement located for Diebold Nixdorf or NCR Atleos.
negative_findings.result_summary: Trade coverage exists for Austria, Portugal and Greece bank deals and for the NCR split into Atleos/Voyix, but nothing HU-specific. Neither vendor appears to run a Hungarian-language newsroom.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The ATM-vendor leg of this cell has no self-published channel in Hungary; leadership moves there will have to be caught via the company registry (nemzeticegtar) and manual LinkedIn review rather than press.

negative_findings.description: No evidence found of Docler Holding acting as a supplier to Hungarian banks.
negative_findings.result_summary: Docler is confirmed as a Luxembourg-headquartered IT/media group with Budapest offices, but nothing connects it to banking or payments delivery. Likewise no ANY Biztonsági Nyomda <-> Nexi Hungary relationship surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Docler should be dropped from this cell's actor map to avoid noise; ANY stays but on card personalisation and transactional print grounds only.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian query terms 'kinevezés' and 'vezető' are heavily polluted by unrelated public-administration and MNB regulatory content.
negative_findings.result_summary: The 4iG appointment query returned MNB decrees, njt.hu legislation and generic AML compliance-officer articles alongside the intended hits.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Production queries must bind the appointment term to a named vendor entity ('4iG' AND 'kinevezés') or add site: constraints; free-floating HU appointment terms will flood the pipeline.

negative_findings.description: LinkedIn is the highest-signal channel for vendor Hungary-lead appointments but is auth-walled and ToS-restricted.
negative_findings.result_summary: Nexi Hungary and other vendor HU pages are indexed and discoverable, but content is not retrievable without login and automated collection is prohibited.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single best signal for this cell's core topic cannot be automated; the run must budget analyst time for manual review or accept a lag via registry-diffing instead.

negative_findings.description: Several vendor root URLs in this slice were inferred from entity names rather than followed link-by-link.
negative_findings.result_summary: cardnet.hu, any.hu, finshape.com, valantic.com and 4ig.hu/hu/sajtoszoba were not individually fetched in this pass; the 4iG domain is confirmed via a 4ig.hu PDF that appeared in results, the others are high-confidence but unfetched.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic liveness pass must resolve these before they are treated as verified; a 404 on a press-room path should trigger a site-root re-crawl rather than a dead-source verdict.

brief: Hungary's private-bank supplier ecosystem is genuinely the only visible half of the transaction, and it splits into three very different source layers. Layer one is statutorily reliable: BÉT and kozzetetelek.mnb.hu disclosures for listed HU vendors (4iG, ANY Biztonsági Nyomda) and the company registries (nemzeticegtar, ceginfo) for officer-level changes at every vendor's Hungarian entity — this is the only route that works for foreign vendors, which publish nothing in Hungarian. Layer two is the HU trade and business press (Bitport, ITBusiness with its EPA PDF backfile, Portfolio tag streams) plus consultancy commentary, above all MINDSPIRE's core-banking transformation blog, which is the single densest pointer into which bank runs which programme with which vendor. Layer three is vendor self-publication — Tietoevry, valantic, Shiwaforce, Finshape, Nexi Central Europe case studies and newsrooms — high-signal but marketing-timed and best snapshot-diffed. The cell's named seed vendors are partly mis-specified for this market: no Temenos/Backbase/Finastra footprint surfaced at OTP, Erste or MBH, the real stack is Flexcube, Intellect iGCB, Tietoevry and Finshape, and the ATM vendors have no Hungarian publication channel at all.
